value.title: Held delivery: steer normal sends mid-turn (F25, C31, F73, F68)
value.summary: Measure how long messages wait behind a busy turn, steer normal sends into a running Copilot turn (C31), flag long holds to the PA, start role-request limits at delivery, and let a reply answer a request.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Messages to a seat in a long turn wait for that turn to end. Today that cost hours (F25). Kestrel found the cause: the Copilot extension claims the next pij message only after the turn the previous one started has ended, though a claimed message already steers. Per ruling C31 this plan steers normal sends into a running Copilot turn as OMP and Pi do (FYIs stay held), with a per-seat off switch and a live wedge canary, keeps the PA's 15-minute held flag as the detector, and makes s12 limits count from delivery (F73), and a reply with --in-reply-to answers a request (F68, moved from plan 212's follow-ups). Owner: delivery (pij-swift-kestrel). Order (prime, 23:25): 214 comes before any further 212 work; it is the biggest drag on the fleet's speed.

sections.name: goals
value: Measure how long messages wait behind a busy turn, steer normal sends into a running Copilot turn (C31), flag long holds to the PA, start role-request limits at delivery, and let a reply answer a request.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Changing FYI semantics or the cold-wake rule.
An --urgent flag (dropped by C31: normal sends steer where a harness can; nothing can where it can't).
Any new delivery timer or poll.

value.claim: Measure held time. For delivery jobs, jobs.enqueued_at is queued, claimed_at is the recipient's claim and acked_at is reached-the-session, on every rung (kestrel, verified: Copilot acks after the host consumes the steered prompt; OMP/Pi after the steer; PTY/UDS after injection). No migration. Held time is enqueued_at to acked_at; a still-queued row has a live age. The PR quotes before and after numbers from the live store.
value.receipt: Before: assets/evidence/cost.md (claim-wait query on the live store, 2026-11-07T11:11Z; no migration, the existing jobs columns). After: the same query once this is deployed.

value.claim: PA flags long holds (C31 keeps it as the detector). The PA digest lists every message held more than 15 minutes behind a busy turn: recipient, sender, msg id, held minutes, and whether it is still queued. Each message is flagged once, not on every digest. The threshold is a named constant.
value.receipt: crates/store/tests/queue.rs: long_holds_are_listed_for_the_pa_once; crates/core/tests/pa_digest.rs: the_digest_lists_messages_held_behind_a_busy_turn; crates/store/src/held.rs: HELD_FLAG_SECS, the_held_read_never_scans_job_history; round 1 (F001): another_fleets_older_holds_never_fill_this_fleets_page

value.claim: C31: normal sends steer mid-turn on Copilot. The Copilot extension keeps claiming pij messages while a turn it started is still running, and steers each normal send into that turn (native.send immediate), as OMP and Pi already do. FYIs stay held until the turn ends, unchanged. A per-seat switch, default on, turns mid-turn steering off for one seat without a release (a daemon-side seat setting, changed by a verb and read by the extension without a restart); with it off, the seat behaves as today. A normal send to a busy seat whose harness can't steer gets a receipt note saying it waits for the turn to end, and why. No --urgent flag: with normal sends steering, it has nothing left to do (see research).
value.receipt: crates/daemon/tests/directory_http.rs: steering_is_switched_per_seat_read_with_the_claim_and_noted_on_receipts; crates/store/src/steering.rs: steering_is_on_until_set_off_and_reports_a_change_once; crates/daemon/src/http/steer.rs: grammar_accepts_on_off_status_with_an_optional_seat; .copilot/extensions/pij/store.test.mjs: the two C31 tests; round 1: a_during_turn_wait_wakes_on_events_and_rechecks_the_switch_at_hand_off (F005, P152-F003), and in store.test.mjs the shared turn watcher (P152-F002) and steered-abort recovery (F003) tests

value.claim: C31 wedge canary (live, required before ready). On a real Copilot seat running one long turn, send 5 normal messages during that turn: each is claimed and steered (claimed_at and acked_at inside the turn), the turn finishes normally, the seat registers idle afterwards, and nothing wedges (an older Copilot build wedged on mid-turn immediate injects: the bg-send wedge history). Then flip the seat's switch off, send once more, and show it waits for turn end. Receipts (msg ids, the store rows, the pane's turn end) go in the evidence.
value.receipt: assets/evidence/steer-canary.md and steer-canary-receipt.json: a real Copilot CLI 1.0.108-1 seat, 5 sends steered inside one long turn, the turn ended and the seat went idle; after pij steer off, one send waited for turn end (local fixture model, no real inference); re-run after round 1 at d8634d6: pass (steer-canary-receipt-r1.json)

value.claim: F73: limits count from delivery. A role request's `--limit` clock starts when the request reaches the holder's session (acked_at), not when it was created; until then the request has no check-in. If a check-in fires, it says how long the request was held in delivery.

F68: a reply answers. A send from the request's holder with `--in-reply-to <request id>` sets the request's answered_at and stops its check-in and escalation; a send without it, or from another seat, does not. `pij output --answers` (s06, live since #137) and this path set the same field, and neither double-counts.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). No new timer, poll or launch. No new store write for held time (existing columns). The PA flag is one indexed query inside the existing PA digest round, constant per digest, not per seat per tick. Claiming during a running turn uses the extension's existing claim call, once per message, not per tick; the per-seat switch is read with that claim, not polled. Measure the live fleet before and after.
value.receipt: Per-site costs and the before readings: assets/evidence/cost.md (no new timer, poll or launch; the switch is read with the claim). After readings follow the deploy.

value.claim: Docs and states. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md: mid-turn steering, the per-seat switch verb, the non-steering receipt note, the held-time fields and the limit clock. Per C31 the pij skill and the pij_send tool description gain one line: choose fyi unless their current work depends on it, since a normal send now interrupts a running turn. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: F25 measured (pm-001, live store, 6 Nov 2026, jobs.enqueued_at to jobs.acked_at for kind delivery:*): 152 of 1,364 deliveries were held over 15 min. pij-local-warbler: 39 of 52 over 15 min, 25 over an hour, max 7.5 h; pij-back-tapir 31 of 48 (max 4 h); pij-swift-kestrel 29 of 38 (max 4 h); pij-wary-lynx 20 of 47 (max 3 h). pm-001's 13:38 to 18:44 sends to warbler reached it between 22:36 and 23:18. That is why #130 needed three asks, and it caused both performance reworks and kestrel's slip. Seams: the daemon queues to Copilot seats with reason extension-stream (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs, enqueue_carrier); the Copilot extension (.copilot/extensions/pij/extension.mjs) only has onUserPromptSubmitted today, which carries held FYIs. The Copilot SDK (copilot-sdk/types.d.ts) has onPostToolUse and onPostToolUseFailure, whose `additionalContext` the host appends as guidance to the model. OMP/Pi already deliver with deliverAs: steer (.omp/extensions/pij/adapters/pi-runtime.ts). Claude delivery is crates/transport/src/uds.rs. F73 (warbler, 23:19): request 01a1b0ab had a 20 min limit, reached warbler at 23:18:55, was answered at 23:18:59 with --in-reply-to, and the check-in still fired at 23:19:16 because the clock ran from creation.

value.question: Does the Claude socket path reach a running turn? If yes, steer there too; if not, Claude gets the receipt note.
value.answer: Yes, already. Busy is the transport's judgement, and Claude's socket transport delivers between tool calls while the seat is Working (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs, the receipt-honesty test's comment, found by u-uds in wave 3). So Claude needs no change here. The receipt note goes to a busy seat whose harness can't take it mid-turn: a pty-only seat, or a Copilot seat with its switch off.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
